assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only 86-eighty-six:rito-oriya@original-light-novels#86-rito-character-reference-profile, the canonical CMR-6 Rito Oriya character reference profile (version 1.2, release 86-V2-V01-V14-1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the locked original-Japanese light novels V01-V14, in which Rito is materially attested from V04, with three audited Alter.1 controls (the perfume-battle material excluded) and Alter.2 excluded. The profile's Appendix A prints all 162 diagnostic rows (86-CMR-RIT-001 to 162) with an exact paragraph route and a Japanese anchor; 16 rows carry a frozen Phase-5 locator and 146 are LOCATOR_GAP rows. V10 has no row. The cumulative locator index, the CMR-9 promotion audit and ledger, the profile's validation and source-verification files, the ledgers L01, L02 and L09, Documents 09 and 12, other characters' profiles, the Phase-5 and Phase-8 artifacts and the Japanese EPUBs are not curated evidence on this subject, and nothing is borrowed from them. The profile's CMR-9 verdict and its High, Moderate and Open labels are inputs, not conclusions. No anime adaptation, V15+ volume or Alter.2 scene is included, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Rito's living states from the earlier Eighty-Six period preserved in Alter.1 (part0013, dependence on Shin (Shinei Nouzen) before independent command; no volume placement) through V04 (Claymore Squadron command, p-006 to p-008), V05 split at the Sirin corpse-road (fear admission to Shin at p-004 ¶36 before; p-009 to p-010 after), V06 split at the located turns (impairment and withdrawal at p-005 ¶449, Shin's offer of a noncombat post and Rito's refusal at p-005 ¶850, the Lyudmila conversation at p-007 ¶398 to ¶455), V07 ensemble scenes, V08 futurity (p-005 ¶122), V09 battalion command split at his injury (p-010 ¶246 to ¶253), V11 split at the Aldrecht confrontation (p-022 ¶236 before; ¶328 to ¶354 after), V12 ordinary recovery and V13 up to his death (Fawn girl refusal at p-007 ¶684 and ¶693; terminal speech at ¶719). There is no living state after V13 p-007; V14 rows are downstream memory and political controls only, and V10 has no row.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The profile gives Rito a causal account: a veteran whose fear of death stays real and becomes articulated choice under fear, while Eighty-Six pride is revised away from compulsory death toward a proliferating future (sections II, IV). It says what changes the response. Recognizable danger compresses talk into rapid local command, while an identity-horror such as the Sirin corpse-road impairs his function (V05 p-009 ¶24; V06 p-005 ¶449 and ¶623). A person directly present interrupts tactical abstraction (V09 p-010 ¶246; the V13 canopy). A grievance offered as someone's whole future meets refusal, especially from a young Eighty-Six (V13 p-007 ¶684, ¶693). A clear tactical reason from a senior is accepted (section XVII). It predicts his mistakes: blurting before organizing a thought, overextension when an exciting solution appears, impairment after trauma, and the V09 hesitation in which the other pilot fired and Rito was wounded. Not A: the predictive section holds eight high-confidence and four moderate predictions without a decision procedure for competing motives; the profile rates overextension and the evolution of his command style Moderate. Not C: the switch variables are located and discriminate between situations.

The profile is built as a developmental state model with located hinges and separates trait from state: his V13 death may not organize his earlier personality (section I). Alter.1 dependence (part0013 ¶18); V04 command with younger-brother energy; V05 fear admission before the Sirin mirror (V05-L002, p-004 ¶36); V06 choice under fear after Shin's offer (V06-L034, p-005 ¶850) and Lyudmila's reframing of fear (V06-L043 to L045); V08 'いろいろ望みたい' (V08-L018, p-005 ¶122); V09 battalion command; V11 claiming Aldrecht (V11-L024, p-022 ¶236); V12 accepting care; V13 the Fawn girl refusal (V13-L104, L105). Not A: V07 holds only ensemble rows, V10 has none, Alter.1 has no volume placement, and the profile rates his further command development Moderate. Not C: each change has a before and after tied to a located scene.

The profile fixes Rito's written-Japanese register. 俺 is the baseline first person, with own-line anchors across states: fear (V05 p-004 ¶36), futurity (V08 p-005 ¶122), command responsibility (V11 p-022 ¶236) and moral refusal with 君 (V13 p-007 ¶684, ¶693). 僕 is a bounded reflective shift in the Lyudmila scene. Terminal おれ is damage-state orthography that may not be used as baseline (¶719). Upward politeness stays casual (隊長, です/ます, りょーかいです). Excitement expands the line, and combat compresses it into short commands such as 散開っ！. Not A: the profile rates the breadth of 僕 Moderate; there is no frequency data; 僕, りょーかいです, 散開っ！ and the V06 '怖いです' refusal are quoted in prose without a printed row, and the row printed beside すげー (V09 p-008 ¶190) is a line addressed to Rito, not his own.

Ordinary life is unusually central in this profile, because his interests define what the future means to him (section IX). Located conduct: carrying shopping and visiting Michihi's room (V07 p-008), canteen talk over fries (V07 p-007 ¶76), fishing with Marcel and Fido (V08 p-005 ¶243), the slip of gossip (V09 p-011 ¶668), visiting the injured Yuto (V09 p-004), Halloween face paint (V12 p-008 ¶660), the canteen exchange (V12 p-004) and watching chess with the cohort (Alter.1 part0041). The stated drivers predict it: permission to be interested, join first and formalize later, and a concrete, sensory and exploratory repair repertoire (library, weird books, cake; section IV.10). Not A: conduct is episodic, with no routine; preferences beyond the attested list are not established.

Eleven directed relations have distinct registers (section VIII). Shin moves from former-command dependence to a commander who claims his own dead (V05 p-004; V11 p-022 ¶236). Raiden stabilizes him without demanding elegant disclosure (Alter.1 part0013). Michihi structures his verbal speed. With Yuto, noisy companionship is care (V09 p-004 ¶252). With Lyudmila, terror becomes dialogue in the softer 僕 register (V06 p-007). Republic civilians are rescued without forgiveness (V11 p-022 ¶339 to ¶354). The Fawn girl is answered face to face with 俺 and 君. Not A: the profile rates reverse-direction states Moderate and says they need the other character's own pass; Theo, Michihi and the Federacy peers are thinly anchored. Not C: the registers differ by relation and are located.

Narrated private states are located at a few points: after Aldrecht he is furious and wants to cry and strikes the screen instead (V11 p-022 ¶354); he finds himself agreeing while trying to deny it (V09 p-010 ¶379); his eager reasoning about the canteen staff (V12 p-004 ¶286); the long silence after which he shakes his head hard (V05 p-006 ¶619). Not B: much of the evidence about him comes from other viewpoints, such as Yuto, Theo, Krena (Kurena Kukumila) and Shin, and the profile's account of his inner life is mainly read from speech. Not D: the narrated states are located and differ by situation.

Combat compresses his talk into command: ambush recognition and dispersal, local improvisation and command after injury (sections V.6, VII; V09 p-008 ¶175 to ¶190, p-010 ¶62). Under trauma he can be impaired and ordered out of the fight, and once regulated he asks not to be excluded (V06 p-005 ¶449, ¶623, ¶850). Recognition of a person interrupts tactical simplicity (V09 p-010 ¶246). He claims a confrontation as his own (V11-L024). Anger at a rescued Republic woman sharpens his speech without turning into revenge (V11 p-022 ¶339 to ¶354). Not A: the profile rates his tactical overextension Moderate and gives no interpersonal conflict among peers beyond banter and correction.

The profile separates four propositions about the Republic: it wronged the Eighty-Six, forgiveness is not required, he no longer needs personal revenge, and he still saves people he does not forgive (section XI). It locates the anti-foreclosure ethic: he refuses the Fawn girl's request for a revenge killing because he does not want grief to make her a killer (V13-L104, L105), and the later mercy killing under an imminent lethal trap is kept separate. It says what decides: a present person, a young Eighty-Six whose grievance threatens to become a whole identity, and the difference between rescue and reconciliation. Not A: the nonforgiveness and いい気味だ statements are quoted in prose without a printed row; his postwar politics are OPEN; the mercy killing is distinguished, not modelled. Not C: the positions are argued, located and discriminate between situations.

The engines are named: he speaks into intensity, as in the reunion joke that Shin has job-changed into a real death god (V04 p-006 ¶175); excitement overflows into silly proposals (the 800 mm bat reply, V09 p-008 ¶255); physical and competitive play with foreign peers across language barriers (V08 and V09); Halloween costume play (V12 p-008 ¶660); and gossip about older comrades. The profile rates humour as a way to defuse mortality tension Moderate. Not A: individual jokes are seldom quoted, and his own comic lines are mostly paraphrased.

A dedicated canonical profile over V04-V14 and Alter.1 whose appendix prints all 162 rows with an exact paragraph route and a Japanese anchor. Sixteen rows carry a frozen Phase-5 locator, and these cover the central hinges: fear, Shin's offer, Lyudmila, futurity, Aldrecht, the Fawn girl and death. Not B: 146 rows are LOCATOR_GAP; many printed anchors are narration that mentions him rather than his own conduct; several central quotations are not among the printed rows; V10 has no row; the narrower authorities the profile defers to are not curated on this subject. Not D: every row has an exact route and anchor across every volume of his life except V10.

Twelve counterexamples are dispositioned and twelve traps listed, with a 'would sound wrong' list (sections XIV to XVI). Located negatives: his fear persists after he chooses to fight (V06 p-005 ¶850), so 'coward becomes brave' is rejected; he refuses removal from combat, so 'pacifist' is rejected; he asks basic strategic and technical questions (V12 p-005 ¶538), so 'strategic genius' is rejected; romance with Lyudmila is OPEN and unsupported; V14 posthumous material may not redefine the living Rito. Not A: the rejection of 'Rito forgives the Republic' rests on prose quotation, not a printed row.

States are placed by volume and paragraph, with hinges at frozen locators (V05-L002 ¶36, V06-L034 ¶850, V08-L018 ¶122, V11-L024 ¶236, V13-L104 ¶684, V13-L106 ¶719), order inside V05, V06, V09, V11 and V13, and a terminal boundary at his death. Not A: V07 and V10 cannot be selected as distinct states, Alter.1 is unplaced except as earlier, and V14 is downstream only. Not C: the located hinges allow a volume to be split at a state change.

conditions: Illustrative textual Japanese only, never quotation, with 俺 as baseline first person; 僕 only in reflective relation-specific speech of the kind located with Lyudmila; terminal おれ never as baseline.
Upward speech keeps 隊長, ranks and です/ます with a loose rhythm; excitement expands the line, combat compresses it into short commands, and fear is voiced rather than hidden.
One living state from V04 to V13 before his death is selected first; no V14 or later state.
No anime performance, frequency distribution or cold strategic abstraction in the register of Lena (Vladilena Milizé).
scenario_readiness.note: Own-line anchors and state deltas constrain illustrative written Japanese in sampled relations; the missing frequency data and prose-only markers restrict form and confidence rather than blocking use.

conditions: Chronology is one explicitly selected living state: Alter.1 earlier dependence; V04; V05 before or after the Sirin corpse-road; V06 after the impairment, after the refusal of removal (p-005 ¶850) or after the Lyudmila conversation (p-007); V08; V09 before or after his injury (p-010 ¶253); V11 before or after Aldrecht (p-022 ¶236); V12; or V13 before the Fawn girl encounter. V07 and V10 are not used as distinct states, and nothing after his death is used.

The interlocutor is a profiled relation in its attested register: Shin (Shinei Nouzen), Raiden (Raiden Shuga), Michihi, Yuto, Lyudmila, his Claymore or Second Battalion unit, foreign peers in shared activity, Republic civilians, or a young Eighty-Six. Theo (Theoto Rikka) and Lena (Vladilena Milizé) are a separate, lower-confidence transfer.

The situation matches a sampled class: a strange technology or creature, a senior's tactical explanation, a frightened peer, his own fear, immediate danger, revenge offered as someone's only future, a question about life after the war, a recovering friend, a known person in an enemy vehicle, or civilians he does not forgive in need of rescue.

Output predicts his characteristic errors: blurting, skipping explanatory steps, tactical overextension and trauma impairment; it never makes him fearless, strategically omniscient or only comic relief.
It abstains on a postwar profession, romance, family, his politics after the war and how his command would have evolved.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One explicitly selected living state between Alter.1 earlier dependence and V13 before the Fawn girl encounter, split at the located hinges: V05 p-004 ¶36 or p-009 to p-010; V06 p-005 ¶449, p-005 ¶850 or p-007; V08 p-005; V09 before or after p-010 ¶253; V11 before or after p-022 ¶236; V12; V13 p-003 to p-006. No V07 or V10 state, no posthumous state and no V15+ material.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Shin (Shinei Nouzen) as former commander and current superior, Raiden (Raiden Shuga) as older stabilizer, Michihi as command peer, Yuto as recovering friend, Lyudmila as an artificial dead soldier he once feared, his own unit, foreign peers, Republic civilians or a young Eighty-Six. Theo (Theoto Rikka), Lena (Vladilena Milizé) and unfamiliar adults are a separate, lower-confidence transfer.
setting_constraints: Federacy bases, Strike Package operations, the Regicide Fleet Countries, Republic territory, the Holy Theocracy front, canteens, hospitals and leisure settings within V04-V13, or Alter.1 cohort scenes without volume placement.
No postwar setting, no romance setting and no institution or technology absent from the V04-V13 corpus.
No terminal-injury state as a basis for ordinary speech or reasoning.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded to sampled relations, situation classes and one explicitly selected living state; his foreclosed futures are excluded rather than inferred.

conditions: Sampled classes only: canteen talk, shopping and errands, fishing, gossip, cards, food exchange and physical games with peers, Halloween and costume play, chess watching, hospital visits and a self-chosen day off of library and cake.
He joins first and talks more than he filters; he asks rather than bluffs about what he does not know.
No invented routine, family life or settled vocation.
scenario_readiness.note: Located ordinary conduct with stated drivers supports bounded extrapolation; the absence of routine blocks READY.

conditions: Situation classes the profile samples: revenge, forgiveness and rescue regarding the Republic; revenge proposed as someone's whole future; a known person inside an enemy vehicle; memorial responsibility for his own dead.
The four Republic propositions stay separate: no forgiveness required, no personal revenge needed, rescue anyway.
The V13 mercy killing is not generalized into a policy and is not substituted for the refused revenge killing.
No postwar politics or abstract political philosophy.
scenario_readiness.note: Argued, located positions support bounded extrapolation in the sampled classes; political philosophy stays outside.

The profile rates romance with Lyudmila OPEN and unsupported, says she should never be romanticized without evidence, and lists no stable romantic partner among the futures it cannot determine. CONDITIONAL would require settling what the profile leaves open.

conditions: His role is squadron commander (V04-V06) or battalion commander (V09-V13) in the Federacy forces and the Strike Package: ambush recognition, dispersal, relief and support movement, local improvisation and command after injury.
He asks strategic and technical questions rather than bluffing, accepts a senior's clear rationale, and may overextend on an exciting solution.
No strategic mastermind role, no staff or political role and no command beyond battalion.
scenario_readiness.note: Located command conduct with stated strengths and limits supports bounded extrapolation within his sampled role.

known_limits.statement: Rito dies in V13 (p-007 ¶719 to ¶744); there is no living state after it, and V14 rows are downstream memory and political controls that the profile says may not redefine who he was.
His death may not be used as the organizing cause of his earlier personality, and the terminal おれ speech belongs to catastrophic brain injury, never to baseline voice.

A postwar profession, a stable romantic partner, a detailed family reconstruction and his politics after the war cannot be determined, and T14-OQ-26 on whether public vindication preserves his particularity is OPEN.
The breadth of the softer 僕 register rests on one relation-specific scene, and reverse-direction relational states need the other character's own profile; the profile rates both Moderate.

The profile is a derived reconstruction reference subordinate to the Japanese source, the Phase-5 and Phase-8 authorities and the canonical V2 ledgers L01, L02 and L09, none of which is curated on this row.

146 of the 162 rows are LOCATOR_GAP, V10 has no row, and several central quotations (the V06 '怖いです' refusal, the 僕 line, the nonforgiveness and いい気味だ statements, 散開っ！ and りょーかいです) have no printed row.
The profile makes no claim about pitch, prosody or performed voice; voice claims cover written Japanese only.
